title: Report quotes scoring_tools.py as evidence reference_verification has weight 0.20 ('most critical predictor') — the cited source says the opposite (weight 0.15, reduced; the quote and the 0.15→0.20 raise describe rental_history)
evidence: Claim (main report, lines 330-331): "**`reference_validator_agent` and the `reference_verification` scoring category (weight 0.20, \"most critical predictor\") already exist** — the scoring-side ingestion is small." and (architecture.md:39-40): "- `reference_verification` is a first-class scoring category; weight raised 0.15 → 0.20 per `tenant_scorer/tools/scoring_tools.py` comment (\"most critical predictor\")." — Cited source (RightTenantryAgents/tenant_scorer/tools/scoring_tools.py, read directly): "# affordability raised 0.20 -> 0.30 (industry 30-40% norm); rental_history # raised 0.15 -> 0.20 (\"most critical predictor\"); reference_verification, # red_flag_detection, application_completeness reduced." and "WEIGHT_REFERENCE_VERIFICATION = 0.15  # Social proof of tenancy reliability"
detail: The verbatim quote and the 0.15→0.20 raise are lifted from a comment about rental_history; reference_verification is actually weighted 0.15 and was reduced. The citation contradicts the claim in both the main report and architecture thread.
recommended_fix: Correct both docs: reference_verification weight is 0.15 (was reduced); the 'most critical predictor' 0.15→0.20 raise applies to rental_history. Keep the existence claims (agent + category verified).
